newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo confirms JCI deal.
newsitem.headline: Anglo confirms JCI deal.

text.p: Anglo American Corp on Monday confirmed it had reached an agreement with the African Mining Group (AMG) consortium for the sale of Anglo's 34.9 percent stake in JCI Ltd.
Anglo and AMG said in a joint statement "that the suspensive conditions relating to the acquisition by the consortium of a significant shareholding in JCI Ltd have been fulfilled".
The statement said these conditions were the satisfactory conclusion of a due diligence investigation and the finalisation of the funding arrangements required by the consortium to buy JCI shares.
It said AMG had obtained irrevocable undertakings to fund the acquisition of 52.8 million JCI shares at 54.50 rand per share.
AMG will hold the investment in JCI through Saflife Ltd which had been agreed -- subject to shareholder approval -- as the investment vehicle for the funding of the deal.
Saflife, through a rights issue or issue of new shares underwritten to the extent of 2.4 billion rand, will be used for the purchase of Anglo's stake in JCI.
The balance of the funding -- about 500 million rand -- will be settled by further issues of Saflife equity and/or preference shares and/or loan finance.
The consortium will pay for the JCI shares on May 2, 1997 and the JCI board will be reconstituted in mid-March under chairmanship of Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd (Captall) chairman Mzi Khumalo.

The AMG consortium will also have a right of first refusal for a period of five years in respect of 12.7 percent of JCI shares being retained by Anglo and its sister company De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd.

AMG -- which groups Captall, African Renaissance Holdings and Khotso Investments among others -- agreed last November to buy a 34.9 percent stake in JCI from Anglo American for 2.88 billion rand or 54.50 rand per share.
The deal gives black business a significant stake in the South African mining industry for the first time.
